Q136341295.summary: An indirect presidential election was held on 17 September 2012 to elect a president to finish the term of Nicholas Liverpool, who resigned. Eliud Williams was elected.

Q365359.label: Mario Echandi Jiménez
Q365359.summary: Mario José Echandi Jiménez was a Costa Rican lawyer and politician who served as the 33rd President of Costa Rica from 1958 to 1962. A conservative liberal, he presided over a process of national reconciliation following the Civil War and modernized the country's drinking water system through the creation of the Costa Rican Institute of Aqueducts and Sewers.

Q552751.desc: Greek politician, prime Minister of Greece, President of New Democracy party

Mitsotakis has been president of the New Democracy party since 2016. He is generally associated with the centre-right, espousing economically liberal policies.

Q259887.label: Christian-Democratic National Peasants' Party
Q259887.summary: The Christian Democratic National Peasants' Party is an agrarian, monarchist and Christian democratic political party in Romania. It claims to be the rightful successor of the interwar National Peasants' Party (PNȚ), created from the merger of the Romanian National Party (PNR) from the then Austro-Hungarian-ruled Transylvania and the Peasants' Party (PȚ) from the Romanian Old Kingdom.

Q111940911.label: 2026 Armenian parliamentary election
Q111940911.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Armenia on 7 June 2026 to elect members of the 9th convocation of the National Assembly. According to exit polls, incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's party Civil Contract won with 56.7% of the vote, followed by the pro-Russian Strong Armenia of Samvel Karapetyan with 17.5%.

Q30335791.label: Finsbury Park incident
Q30335791.img: Finsbury Park Station Seven Sisters Road geograph-3880584-by-Ben-Brooksbank.jpg
Q30335791.summary: On 19 June 2017, an Islamophobic terrorist attack occurred in Finsbury Park, London, England, when a van was intentionally driven into a crowd of Muslim pedestrians near the Muslim Welfare House, 100 yards (90 m) from the Finsbury Park Mosque, resulting in the death of a man and 11 injuries. The attack was found to be motivated by Islamophobia.

Q13403439.label: Battle of Mount Song
Q13403439.desc: 1944 battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War
Q13403439.img: Camouflaged and poorly equipped Chinese soldiers repell a charge of 50,000 Japanese along the Salween River near Burma. - DPLA - 57d615b363887a1f241f81440e052fb7.gif
Q13403439.summary: The Battle of Mount Song, also known as the Battle of Ramou (拉孟の戦い), in 1944 was part of a larger campaign in southwest China during the Second World War. Chinese Nationalist forces aimed to retake the Burma Road.

Q713519.label: Saar Offensive
Q713519.desc: French ground operation into Saarland from 7 to 16 September 1939
Q713519.summary: The Saar Offensive was the French invasion of Saarland, Germany, in the first stages of World War II, from September 7 to October 16, 1939, in response to the German invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939. The original plans called for 40 divisions, one armored division, three mechanised divisions, 78 artillery regiments and 40 tank battalions to assist Poland, which was then under invasion, by attacking Germany's neglected western front. Despite 30 divisions advancing to the border, the attack did not have the expected result.

Q1891631.label: Battle for The Hague
Q1891631.desc: 1940 battle in the Second World War
Q1891631.summary: The Battle for The Hague took place on 10 May 1940 during the Battle of the Netherlands. German Fallschirmjäger units were dropped in and around The Hague to capture Dutch airfields and the city itself.

Q3273519.label: Naval Battle of Casablanca
Q3273519.desc: 1942 naval engagements during WW II invasion of North Africa
Q3273519.summary: The Naval Battle of Casablanca was a series of naval engagements fought between American ships covering the invasion of North Africa and Vichy French ships defending the neutrality of French Morocco in accordance with the Second Armistice at Compiègne during World War II. Allied military planners anticipated an all-American force assigned to seize the Atlantic port city of Casablanca might be greeted as liberators. An invasion task force of 102 American ships carrying 35,000 American soldiers approached the Moroccan coast undetected under cover of darkness.

Q7097647.label: Operation Tomahawk
Q7097647.summary: Operation Tomahawk was an airborne military operation by the 187th Regimental Combat Team on 23 March 1951 at Munsan-ni as part of Operation Courageous in the Korean War. Operation Courageous was designed to trap large numbers of Chinese People's Volunteer Army (PVA) and Korean People's Army (KPA) forces between the Han and Imjin Rivers north of Seoul, opposite the Republic of Korea Army (ROK) I Corps.

Q7097135.label: Operation Hickory
Q7097135.desc: United states military operation during the Vietnam war
Q7097135.img: Map of Operations Hickory, Belt Tight, Beau Charger and Lam Son 54.jpg
Q7097135.summary: Operation Hickory was a search and destroy operation conducted by the 3rd Marine Division in the area around Con Thien, Quảng Trị Province known as Leatherneck Square from 18 to 28 May 1967. Operation Hickory was the first authorized incursion into the Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).

Q47510319.label: Battle of Aden (2018)
Q47510319.desc: conflict between the STC and the Hadi-led government
Q47510319.summary: The Battle of Aden was a conflict between the Southern Transitional Council (STC) and the Yemeni government around the headquarters in Aden.

Q380719.label: Cotton Mather
Q380719.desc: American religious minister and scientific writer (1663–1728)
Q380719.summary: Cotton Mather was a Puritan theologian in British America. After being educated at Harvard College, he joined his father Increase Mather as minister of the Congregationalist Old North Meeting House in Boston, then part of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, where he preached for the rest of his life. Active in local politics, Cotton Mather was also a prolific author who covered theological, historical, and scientific subjects. That work established Mather as a major intellectual and public figure in English-speaking colonial America.

mentions.c: Onesimus’s inoculation saves lives in Boston (1721)

Q44335.label: Keith Campbell
Q44335.desc: British biologist (1954-2012) Professor of Animal Development at the University of Nottingham
Q44335.summary: Keith Henry Stockman Campbell was a British biologist who was a member of the team at Roslin Institute that in 1996 first cloned a mammal, a Finnish Dorset lamb named Dolly, from fully differentiated adult mammary cells. He was Professor of Animal Development at the University of Nottingham. In 2008, he received the Shaw Prize for Medicine and Life Sciences jointly with Ian Wilmut and Shinya Yamanaka for "their works on the cell differentiation in mammals".

Q1525551.label: Party of the Cuban People – Orthodox
Q1525551.summary: The Party of the Cuban People – Orthodox, commonly shortened to the Orthodox Party, was a Cuban left-wing populist political party. It was founded in 1947 by Eduardo Chibás in response to government corruption and lack of reform. Its primary aims were the establishment of a distinct national identity, economic independence and the implementation of social reforms.

Q29999.label: Kingdom of the Netherlands
Q29999.desc: transcontinental sovereign state and constitutional monarchy
Q29999.summary: The Kingdom of the Netherlands, commonly known simply as the Netherlands, is a sovereign state consisting of a collection of constituent territories united under the monarch of the Netherlands, who functions as head of state. The realm is a unitary monarchy with its largest subdivision, the eponymous Netherlands, predominantly located in Northwestern Europe and with three smaller island territories located in the Caribbean.
